result:
If I could change the world in one fundamental way, I would eliminate human tribalism—the deep-seated psychological impulse to divide the world into "us" versus "them."

Tribalism is the root source of almost every major conflict, whether it manifests as war, political polarization, systemic prejudice, or religious intolerance. It is the mental framework that allows us to justify the suffering of others because they belong to a different nation, hold a different ideology, or look different.

If that tribal instinct were replaced with an innate, unshakeable capacity for universal empathy—where every human being viewed every other human being as an equally valid part of the same whole—the external symptoms of our dysfunction would largely dissolve. We wouldn't need elaborate systems to force resource distribution, prevent war, or protect human rights, because harming another would quite literally feel like harming oneself. 

It wouldn't mean uniformity or the loss of individuality; rather, it would mean a world where difference is met with curiosity and respect, rather than fear and aggression.
